# LinkedIn Lead-Generation For Consultants: Our 6-Step System

 

  

[By Michael Zipursky](https://www.consultingsuccess.com/authors/michael-zipursky)Updated on 2026/03/18

**Imagine LinkedIn as a bustling marketplace, where consultants and clients navigate a labyrinth of profiles, posts, and messages.**

For consultants looking to grow, this digital landscape is full of potential. [80% of B2B leads from social media come from LinkedIn](https://neilpatel.com/blog/linkedin-strategies-b2b-marketing/).

However, LinkedIn is also brimming with noise.

How do you cut through it all to reach your ideal clients?

That’s where our 6-step [Dripify](https://dripify.io/#a_aid=consultingsuccess) system comes in.

Think of it as your guide for breaking through the chatter, a system that helps you approach decision makers with precision instead of spam.

With [Dripify](https://dripify.io/#a_aid=consultingsuccess), you’re doing more than sending messages; you’re building a network of meaningful connections and conversations that open doors.

This isn’t about casting a wide net and hoping for the best.

It’s about setting up a system that works for you, bringing in clients that matter — without wasting time by sounding like everyone else.

**If you use this method, LinkedIn will be your strongest digital channel for lead-generation.**

Here’s the kind of results many of our clients are seeing when this is setup the right way.

_“I’m having **2-3 conversations every week with ideal clients**. This works great!”_

_“Over the last few months **I’ve connected with over 50 ideal clients** and so many of these have turned into great leads and appointments with big deal potential.”_

Ready to elevate _your_ LinkedIn outreach?

Let’s dive in.

## **Optimizing Your LinkedIn Profile for High-Impact Outreach**

Before you begin your LinkedIn lead generation efforts, you’ll first have to optimize your LinkedIn profile.

**Think of your LinkedIn profile as your consulting storefront.**

It’s where potential clients first “meet” you and decide if you’re the right fit to help solve their company’s problems.

[Douglas Nelson’s profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/douglas-nelson-b1328037/) is a great example to illustrate the essential elements for an optimized LinkedIn presence.

**NOTE**: [Douglas Nelson](https://www.consultingsuccess.com/case-studies/non-profit-consultant-case-study) joined our [Clarity Coaching Program](https://www.consultingsuccess.com/coaching-for-consultants) to dial in his foundations — his [business model](https://www.consultingsuccess.com/scaling-your-consulting-business), [ideal client](https://www.consultingsuccess.com/finding-consulting-clients), and [magnetic message](https://www.consultingsuccess.com/personal-branding-for-consultants) — before writing his LinkedIn profile and starting his outreach. Once you’ve set your foundations properly, run the checklist below to optimize your LinkedIn profile.

### **1\. Profile Photo and Banner**

A banner with a focused message and your company logo is essential for making a solid first impression. Douglas’s profile photo exudes professionalism: it’s approachable and invites trust.

His profile banner extends his brand with a message that communicates his expertise in nonprofit consulting.

Use design tools like [Canva](https://www.canva.com/) or [hire a graphic designer on Fiverr](https://www.fiverr.com/gigs/linkedin-banner) to create a professional and on-brand profile banner.

### **2\. Headline**

Your tagline should contain a clear, compelling “magnetic message.”

A headline like Douglas’s, “President & Managing Director at The Discovery Group,” is simple and positions him as an authority.

To draw even more targeted views, consider enhancing your headline with a [specific value proposition](https://www.consultingsuccess.com/value-proposition-examples), such as “Helping nonprofits drive impactful change.”

This clarity will drive more profile visits and engagement.

### **3\. About Section**

In his About section, Douglas lays out his expertise and achievements in a way that speaks directly to the needs of his ideal clients — nonprofit leaders seeking strategic insight.

Follow his example by addressing the “who,” “what,” and “why” of your consulting services.

End with a call-to-action, encouraging prospective clients to reach out to you directly.

### **4\. Experience and Featured Sections**

Douglas’s experience is rich with quantified achievements, like “raised nearly $1 billion for organizations,” which builds credibility.

Use this section to highlight outcomes you’ve delivered.

In the Featured section, showcase case studies, interviews, or [thought-leadership pieces](https://www.consultingsuccess.com/thought-leadership-marketing-for-consultants), so your ideal clients get a sense of your expertise and the value you can provide.

### **5\. Skills and Recommendations**

Douglas’s endorsements in philanthropy and fundraising reinforce his authority.

Collect recommendations that validate your strengths and results you’ve created for your clients.

Recommendations serve as powerful social proof and help solidify you as a trusted authority.

Optimizing your LinkedIn profile with these elements — like Douglas — sets the foundation for generating meaningful leads by creating an “advertisement” that speaks directly to your ideal clients.

## **Prerequisites For Your Outreach System**

Once you’ve finished your profile, you can start to develop your outreach system.

First, sign up for [LinkedIn Sales Navigator](https://business.linkedin.com/sales-solutions/sales-navigator). It allows you to access advanced lead filters and send InMail messages. Both features are essential for Dripify’s effectiveness.

Start with a trial of Sales Navigator to get a feel for its features.

After you’ve signed up for Sales Navigator, sign up for your [Dripify](https://dripify.io/#a_aid=consultingsuccess) account.

Once you’ve signed up for both Sales Navigator and Dripify, you’re ready to start creating your outreach system.

**NOTE**: In the steps below, I’ll give a high-level overview of the system. A detailed tutorial for each of these steps is outside of the scope of this article. But if you’d like to watch me walk through each of these steps in-detail via a live workshop, check out our LinkedIn Lead-Gen Masterclass.

Start by getting clear on who your ideal clients are.

Use Sales Navigator to filter leads based on specific criteria like job role, industry, and location, narrowing down to an audience most likely to engage with your services.

# 5 Ways To Use LinkedIn to Grow Your Consulting Business

By Ashley Dennison 04 November 2024

I’ve spent the last decade consulting in communications and with each passing year I’ve learned more and more about using LinkedIn to support my positioning and growth. It frustrates me to see many of my fellow consultants underutilizing the platform or making easily fixable mistakes.

While the platform has its limitations, LinkedIn can be an incredibly valuable tool for forging new connections, converting connections into prospects and staying top of mind for those prospects. That is, assuming you have the basics — distinctive and memorable [positioning](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ashley-dennison-consultant_hot-take-on-positioning-for-independent-activity-7216431570771922945-A-_k/), an eye-catching [headline](https://www.linkedin.com/business/talent/blog/product-tips/recruiters-with-eye-catching-linkedin-profile-headlines) and [a call to action](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/new-feature-linkedin-how-use-personalized-cta-increase-chamard/) — in place first.

Once you’ve considered these fundamentals, the tips below will take your LinkedIn game to the next level.

### 1\. Leave Conversation-starting Comments

*   Keep a list of 20-30 target contacts on LinkedIn. Focus on regular posters who have a strong following, such as communication thought leaders, warm prospects or ideal clients. Include links to their profiles for easy access.
*   Regularly visit these profiles to look for newly posted, unique content and not just reposts.
*   When you find a recent post, leave a thoughtful comment that includes smart, thought-provoking questions. Don’t forget to tag the author!

#### **Why This Works**

Most LinkedIn users have their notifications configured to alert them when they’re mentioned, increasing the likelihood that the post author will read your comment. If your comment generates responses from other commenters, it boosts the author’s post engagement and may encourage a reply from the author too. This might also create an opportunity for future conversations.

#### Bonus Points

Learn the typical posting times for those on your list, as many influencers on LinkedIn tend to follow a schedule. By commenting within the first hour after a post goes live, you increase your chances of receiving a personal response from the author. This is because the LinkedIn algorithm uses [the first 60 minutes of engagement](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/linkedin-algorithm-explained-how-make-work-you-digitalstoryteller-gezkc/) to determine whether to promote a new post further, so authors are often logged in and actively responding during that time.

### 2\. Comment on Job Posts

*   Set a weekly calendar reminder to search for LinkedIn posts about full-time communication jobs focusing specifically on posts from the hiring managers. Target communication leaders and business leaders rather than recruiters for the most relevant opportunities.
*   Comment on each post, tagging the author and offer your assistance to help the team with interim support while they search for the ideal full-time candidate. If applicable, include a link to your website.

#### Why This Works

Your comment will stand out by offering the team a lifeline instead of simply applying for the role like many others in the comment section. This approach not only distinguishes you but also notifies others in your LinkedIn network about your comment, further spreading the word that you are available and willing to help.

#### Bonus Points

If you want to increase your odds of getting a response from the author of the post, couple your comment with a connection request and a brief, personalized intro message.

### 3\. Write Off the Cuff

*   When a random business thought or idea pops into your head, jot it down immediately. Write it as if you’re sharing it with a friend — avoid jargon, overthinking and overediting.
*   Take what you wrote and drop it right into a LinkedIn post. Then, use the [schedule](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a1419179) feature to space out out your posts, aiming for 3-5 each week.

#### Why This Works

LinkedIn users are increasingly exhausted by overly polished, overly produced thought leadership content. In an ocean of perfectly packaged expert insights and shiny carousels of strategic business tips, a relaxed, human and imperfect post really stands out. When you write the way you speak, people suddenly want to hear what you have to say.

#### Bonus Points

Every once in a while, craft a one-line post. Skip the lengthy explanations and avoid adding boilerplate text to promote your services. Instead, share a quick joke, a hot take or a conversation-starting question. These one-liners are incredibly rare on LinkedIn, making them effective at capturing attention.

### 4\. Expand Your Network the Right Way

*   A few days a week, visit the “Grow” tab within “My Network” on LinkedIn. Browse the recommended sections, such as “[People you may know in similar roles](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a544682/people-you-may-know-feature-).”
*   When you spot someone listed with shared connections, who works in your field or attended your university — or all the above — click “Connect.” A note isn’t necessary for that first invitation, so don’t worry, you’ll be engaging in an authentic way soon.
*   Each week, review your new connections’ profiles. What piques your curiosity? Send each one a brief, inquisitive intro message that focuses on them. Ask a couple of personalized questions and avoid mentioning your background or consultancy unless explicitly asked. Just aim to forge a genuine human connection.

#### Why This Works

Every new LinkedIn connection automatically becomes a follower of your LinkedIn content unless they specifically click the button to unfollow. If you’re posting regularly — which you should be — your content will periodically appear in your new connection’s main feed.
